title: Big Bang NOT NULL Constraint Rollout
damaged_code:
```sql
-- Migration script executed in Database before app upgrade finishes rolling out
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN first_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL;
```
pattern: Adding a new column with a `NOT NULL` constraint to a shared database schema before all instances of the application code have been upgraded to write that field.
why_bad: Older application instances currently running in production do not know about the new column. When they attempt to perform `INSERT` operations during the rolling upgrade, the database will reject the queries with constraint violations, causing write downtime [793].
detection: Any migration script containing a `NOT NULL` constraint on a newly added column without a default value, deployed while older application code is still serving write traffic.
counterexample: None. Adding non-nullable fields without defaults during live operations always breaks backwards compatibility.
fix:
Perform schema updates in three distinct phases: first, add the column as nullable (Expansion Phase); second, upgrade all application code to write the field; third, backfill historical data and add the `NOT NULL` constraint (Cleanup Phase) [793, 794].
```sql
-- Phase 1: Expansion (Add column as nullable)
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN first_name VARCHAR(255);
```
source: Release It!, "Adaptable Enterprise Architecture - Zero-Downtime Deployment" [383, 384, 793, 794]
